tier_reason: First-party table in README.md produced by the public harness scripts/bench.sh (hyperfine -N, 3 warmups, 20 runs, 48 decodes per invocation) with tools/libwebpdec.c driving libwebp at pinned revision 94d3c4a (decoder version 1.6.0). The CPU (Intel Core i7-13700K) is named only in the README at commit 64273a2 and in the since-deleted AVX2_BENCHMARKS.md, and no rustc, C compiler or NASM version is given anywhere, so it falls short of A.

corrections.baseline: libwebp at pinned revision 94d3c4a (decoder version 1.6.0), static libwebpdecoder plus libwebpdemux built through Meson's CMake subproject, single-threaded
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-13700K, Linux x86-64, benchmark pinned to CPU 0 (named in the README at commit 64273a2 and in AVX2_BENCHMARKS.md at commit 0a453d8; the 2026-10-01 README reformat 85e77ee dropped the machine paragraph but kept the same table numbers)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Meson release build (default buildtype=release, assembly enabled, -Dtrim_dsp=false); Rust release profile with lto=fat, codegen-units=1 and opt-level 3 for dependencies (Cargo.toml); libwebp built through the Meson CMake subproject (libwebp's CMake default build type is Release); rustc, C compiler and NASM versions are not stated
corrections.workload: Median wall-clock time of one process doing 48 decodes (hyperfine -N, 3 warmups, 20 runs; wpd --threads 1, libwebp use_threads off; output discarded to /dev/null but the requested format conversion still runs) on 7 files from halidecx/wpd-test-data. Both decoders request the same output format per row: planar YUV420P/YUVA420P for lossy stills, RGBA for lossless stills and composited animations. Decode defaults match libwebp's (loop filtering and fancy upsampling on). image-webp 0.2.4 appears only in RGBA rows.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (median ms per 48-decode run, libwebp / wpd): lossy.webp YUV420P 180.40/173.56 = 1.04x; simplelf-lossy.webp YUV420P 174.43/162.07 = 1.08x; anim_yuv.webp RGBA 190.90/169.18 = 1.13x; lossless.webp RGBA 195.75/111.27 = 1.76x; anim_rgb.webp RGBA 104.47/62.56 = 1.67x; a_lossy.webp YUVA420P 50.70/36.38 = 1.39x; anim_yuva.webp RGBA 494.37/374.46 = 1.32x. image-webp is slower than libwebp on every RGBA row (e.g. lossless 231.50 ms, anim_yuva 776.54 ms). With both decoders forced to RGBA on the same machine (AVX2_BENCHMARKS.md at commit 0a453d8) the lossy stills give 195.16/189.38 = 1.03x (lossy.webp), 188.91/179.66 = 1.05x (simplelf-lossy.webp) and 71.78/60.37 = 1.19x (a_lossy.webp).
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers on very fresh code: measured 2026-09-30 on wpd 59a1c12 plus then-uncommitted AVX2 changes (landed as a78b2c4 on 2026-10-01). Lossy stills gain only 1.04x-1.08x (1.03x-1.05x when both output RGBA); the larger wins are lossless (1.76x) and animation (1.13x-1.67x). Earlier README tables showed much larger ratios: the 2.38x and 4.56x figures in the search snippet come from the c91dc1e table (2026-09-17) and are relative to image-webp, not libwebp (libwebp/wpd in that table is 1.10x-1.85x, derived from page data); the f5c5b33 table gave libwebp/wpd 1.26x-3.07x (derived from page data); the 54d03ee table, run before f5c5b33 pinned wpd to one thread, reached 17.19x versus image-webp. Those runs were on an Apple M5 Pro and the old scripts/bench.sh asked libwebp and image-webp for RGBA while wpd emitted its native output (planar YUV for lossy), so wpd skipped the YUV-to-RGB conversion the baselines performed. Commit 0a453d8 ('bench: compare matching formats and expose libwebp threading') fixed the harness, and AVX2_BENCHMARKS.md states that the corrected x86 numbers miss the old ARM ratios on six of seven images. The current README still says 'reproduce the CPU affinity above' although the machine line was removed. Test files live in a separate repo (halidecx/wpd-test-data). Language is Rust plus hand-written assembly (NASM on x86, ARM/AArch64 directories) with a C ABI (include/wpd.h); C appears only in headers, tools and test harnesses. It is not C++, so it falls outside the C++ language filter, but C++ code can call it through wpd.h. The LICENSE file (BSD-2-Clause) was only added on 2026-10-03; Cargo.toml declared BSD-2-Clause earlier.

notes: Numbers match the current README exactly; the drop from the earlier 2.38x-4.56x table is explained by a harness fix (matching output formats, one thread) plus a move from Apple M5 Pro to i7-13700K, not by a regression. Please set language to 'Rust and assembly, C ABI (wpd.h)' via decisions (language is not a correctable field here); the record's current language string is accurate.

tier_reason: First-party criterion run of the public benchmarks/benches/decode_png.rs, summarized in benchmarks/benchmark-results.md (commit 0875e77, 2026-09-21) for an unnamed Darwin machine with no CPU model or compiler version, so C. Downgraded on the claim, not the tier: the spng side is a handicapped 2021 build doing different checksum work.

corrections.baseline: libspng 0.6.3 through the Rust spng 0.1.0 binding (spng-sys 0.1.0, 2021) linked to bundled stock zlib via libz-sys (zlib-ng feature off); libpng is not measured
corrections.claimed_speedup: benchmarks/benchmark-results.md (Darwin, criterion mean, ms; spng vs zune-png): baseline 297.4 vs 135.0 (spng 2.20x slower, as printed); interlaced 8bpp 378.0 vs 139.7 (2.71x, as printed); 16 bpp 541.2 vs 186.3 (2.9x, derived from page data); palette 53.59 vs 35.21 (1.5x, derived from page data). image-rs/png beats zune-png on 16 bpp (163.7 ms; zune 1.14x slower) and palette (28.31 ms; zune 1.24x slower). These ratios overstate the library gap: the spng side is libspng 0.6.3 (2021) on stock zlib with its ARM NEON path disabled, and it verifies chunk CRCs while zune-png verifies neither CRC nor Adler-32.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench with criterion 0.8.1 (20 s measurement time) under the workspace bench profile (release opt-level 3 plus debug info, no target-cpu flags); libspng compiled by the cc crate in spng-sys build.rs (SPNG_SSE defined only for x86 targets with ssse3/sse4.1); rustc and C compiler versions not stated
corrections.hardware: Unnamed Darwin (macOS) machine; CPU model not given (the benchmarks README's Homebrew /opt/homebrew setup suggests Apple Silicon). The benchmarks README also lists an AMD EPYC-Rome KVM Linux box, but the results file has only Darwin columns.
corrections.workload: Criterion decode from an in-memory buffer of four PNG files from the zune-image test-images set (speed_bench.png, speed_bench_interlaced.png, speed_bench_16.png, speed_bench_palette.png), one thread per decode for all three libraries: zune-png decode_raw with default DecoderOptions, image-rs/png 0.18.0-rc.3 with EXPAND and ignore_checksums(true), and the spng 0.1.0 binding with Format::Png (native layout), TRANSPARENCY and IGNORE_ADLER32. Outputs are not cross-checked, and their layouts differ.
corrections.caveats: The measured code does different work from the baseline. Checksums: zune-png's default options skip both chunk CRC and zlib Adler-32 checks, image-rs/png is told to ignore both, but spng only ignores Adler-32 and keeps libspng's default CRC verification of critical chunks (crc_action_critical = SPNG_CRC_ERROR). Baseline build: the spng crate pinned is 0.1.0 from March 2021 with libspng 0.6.3 (current libspng is 0.7.x), linked to stock zlib through libz-sys with the zlib-ng option off, and its ARM NEON unfilter path is commented out in that libspng version, so on an Apple machine spng runs scalar filters on stock zlib inflate. Output layouts differ: spng's Format::Png returns native rows (palette indices with tRNS not applied, host-endian 16-bit samples), while zune-png and image-rs expand palettes to RGB(A) and keep 16-bit samples big-endian. libpng, the category incumbent, is not measured at all. Single results file, Apple hardware, no CPU model, criterion timings on the maintainer's own image set. In the same file zune-jpeg is slower than mozjpeg on most cases (1.1x-1.3x slower on baseline and subsampled decodes, about 1.0x-1.1x faster only on some progressive cases), zune-inflate is 1.5x-2.5x slower than libdeflate, and zune-qoi is 1.88x slower than rapid-qoi, so the claim holds only for PNG against this spng build, not for the zune family generally. The README only promises 'on par with or better than reference libraries'. Language is Rust; a C API exists in crates/zune-capi (library name zil_c, wrapping zune-image), so it sits outside the C++ language filter unless used through that C API.

notes: Numbers match the page; downgraded because the spng comparison is not like-for-like (old libspng 0.6.3 on stock zlib, CRC verified on spng only, NEON off). Please set language to 'Rust (C API via crates/zune-capi)' via decisions; language is not a correctable field here.
